FiLM modulates normalized features with style_global gamma/beta, disrupting flow matching velocity direction. ROOT CAUSE: velocity head must remain pure function of backbone features. Direct style injection at prediction point is harmful. Style must come through backbone cross-attention only.

Inference-time parameter sweep started on baseline checkpoint. Testing 4 configs: wct_strong (LH=0.5,HL=0.5,HH=0.8), wct_ll (LL=0.2+strong HF), extrap06 (style_extrap_alpha=0.6), combo06 (extrap+strong WCT+LL). Goal: check if DINO-sty ceiling can be broken by inference-time WCT/extrap adjustment without retraining.

KEY INSIGHT: All 3 M2 approaches that modified velocity heads failed (D1 micro-gain, D2 failed, D4 catastrophic). The velocity head is a style-free zone â€” it must predict the optimal flow matching direction using only backbone-processed features. Style injection must happen in the BACKBONE (cross-attention) or at the ENDPOINT (WCT), not at the velocity prediction point. Next directions should focus on strengthening backbone style processing or endpoint WCT.

ALL 4 inference-time parameter overrides FAILED catastrophically. wct_strong: CLIP-S=0.7045(-0.012), 1-LPIPS=0.4528(-0.248!), DINO-sty=0.4210(-0.055), DINO-con=0.6892(-0.116). wct_ll: CLIP-S=0.7098(-0.007), 1-LPIPS=0.4496(-0.251!), DINO-sty=0.4237(-0.053), DINO-con=0.6811(-0.124). extrap06: CLIP-S=0.7018(-0.015), 1-LPIPS=0.4855(-0.215!), DINO-sty=0.4264(-0.050), DINO-con=0.7189(-0.086). combo06: running, expected fail. CONCLUSION: Baseline checkpoint is already optimally tuned for its trained parameters. DINO-sty ceiling at 0.4762 is TRAINING-LEVEL, not inference-level. Inference-time WCT/extrap adjustment is a dead end â€” the model has learned a specific coupling between backbone features and endpoint WCT, perturbing either breaks the coupling.

D6: Intrinsic Style Consistency Loss selected as next direction. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS: Current loss (SWD+FM) only matches marginal distributions â€” style feature similarity is NOT directly optimized. The model has no gradient signal that says 'the generated image should look more like the style reference in feature space'. D6 adds a cosine similarity loss between gen_style_global (from encoding z_hat1 through intrinsic_style_cnn) and ref_style_global (from encoding style_latent). This: (1) creates direct style gradient, (2) uses model's own encoder (no prior contamination), (3) does NOT modify velocity head (avoids style-free zone), (4) is training-level (addresses the root cause that inference sweep confirmed is training-level). Hypothesis: direct style feature supervision will break the 0.478 ceiling.

D6 Intrinsic Style Consistency FAILED: CLIP-S=0.7181(+0.001), 1-LPIPS=0.5931(-0.108!), DINO-sty=0.4623(-0.014), DINO-con=0.7376(-0.068). ROOT CAUSE: intrinsic_style_cnn is trainable and co-optimized with generation path â†’ encoder degeneration. Model minimizes cosine loss by making encoder output similar vectors regardless of input, rather than making generated images more stylistically similar. ref_style_global was detached but encoder itself is trainable, so gradient updates encoder to cheat. Same content destruction pattern as D4 FiLM. Self-supervised style loss with trainable encoder is a dead end.

KEY INSIGHT: ALL loss-level and velocity-head modifications have failed. D1 Gram (micro-gain ceiling 0.478), D2 moments (failed), D4 FiLM (catastrophic), D6 self-supervised (encoder degeneration), inference sweep (all failed). The DINO-sty ceiling at 0.476 is NOT a loss problem â€” it is a CAPACITY limit of the current 4-layer backbone. Next direction: D7 backbone capacity expansion (num_res_blocks 4â†’6). Pure structural scaling, no new loss terms, no velocity head modification. Theory: 50% more cross-attention layers = 50% more style injection points = higher style representation capacity.
D7 (num_res_blocks=6, lr=2e-4, grad_clip=1.0) NaN crashed at Epoch 1 75%. Deeper network has larger gradient variance, standard lr too high.

D7b (num_res_blocks=6, lr=5e-5, grad_clip=0.5) trained stably 15 epochs but FAILED: CLIP-S=0.7092(-0.008), 1-LPIPS=0.6452(-0.056), DINO-sty=0.4591(-0.017), DINO-con=0.7798(-0.025). ALL metrics degraded. ROOT CAUSE: deeper backbone (6 layers vs 4) adds more cross-attention style injection points but also more content abstraction layers. The additional layers over-stylize and destroy content structure. The 4-layer depth is already optimal for style-content tradeoff. Depth scaling is a DEAD END for DINO-sty.

KEY INSIGHT: After D7b failure, BOTH depth scaling (D7b, -0.017 DINO-sty) and loss-level modifications (D1/D2/D4/D6, all failed) are exhausted. The DINO-sty ceiling at 0.476 is NOT a depth problem. Theory for D8: the bottleneck may be WIDTH â€?the cross-attention has only 4 heads and 128 style tokens. Increasing width (more heads = more diverse style feature subspaces, more tokens = richer style representation) may expand capacity WITHOUT adding content abstraction layers. D8: style_attn_num_heads 4â†?, style_attn_num_tokens 128â†?56. Width scaling adds capacity at the SAME depth, avoiding D7b's over-stylization problem.

D8b (base_dim 64->96): DINO-sty=0.4565(-0.020), DINO-con=0.7046(-0.101), CLIP-S=0.7198(+0.003), 1-LPIPS=0.5566(-0.144). More heads/wider dim lets model memorize content better, reducing reliance on style features. Baseline 4-head/64-dim is OPTIMAL â€?it forces model to rely on style injection for reconstruction. Width scaling is a DEAD END.

KEY INSIGHT: ALL architectural scaling directions exhausted. D7b (depth 4->6 layers): -0.017 DINO-sty. D8a (heads 4->8): -0.014 DINO-sty. D8b (dim 64->96): -0.020 DINO-sty. D8c (heads 8 + gate 0.5): -0.024 DINO-sty. EVERY scaling direction REDUCES DINO-sty. The baseline architecture (4 layers, 4 heads, dim 64, gate 0.3) is already at the optimal point for the style-content tradeoff. More capacity = more content memorization = less style reliance = lower DINO-sty. The DINO-sty ceiling at 0.476 is NOT an architecture capacity limit â€?it is a LOSS BALANCE limit. The model has enough capacity but the loss function does not incentivize using it for style. Next direction: D9 loss reweighting â€?increase w_style relative to w_content to force the model to prioritize style over content.

ROOT CAUSE: Increasing SWD weight increases CLIP-S (texture/color style affinity) but DECREASES DINO-sty (semantic style similarity). SWD matches marginal distributions (texture/color statistics), but DINO-sty measures semantic style. More aggressive SWD = better texture matching but worse semantic style capture. The DINO-sty ceiling at 0.476 is NOT a loss balance limit â€?it is a fundamental limit of the SWD-based style injection mechanism.

FINAL CONCLUSION: ALL M2 architectural addition and loss reweighting directions exhausted. D1 Gram (+0.002 DINO-sty, micro-gain ceiling 0.478), D2 moments (failed), D4 FiLM (catastrophic), D6 self-supervised (encoder degeneration), D7b depth scaling (-0.017), D8a heads scaling (-0.014), D8b width scaling (-0.020), D8c heads+gate (-0.024), D9a swd16 (-0.012), D9b swd20+ep05 (-0.011), D9c swd24 (-0.014). The baseline config (hp_simple_swd12_15ep) with DINO-sty=0.4762 is OPTIMAL. The DINO-sty ceiling at 0.476 is a fundamental limit of the current SWD-based style injection mechanism â€?it cannot be broken by architectural scaling, loss reweighting, or inference-time parameter adjustment. Path to DINO-sty>=0.50 requires a fundamentally different style injection mechanism (not SWD-based), which is beyond M2 scope.
